title: The lifecycle row reads a coded run outcome, and each warning offers its fix
deviations_from_card: (1) Halt/cancel outcome: facts carry only what the step counted ({evaluated} in the drain, {promoted} in the promote loop), and a halt after failed evaluations carries warnings [{eval_failed,n}] rather than [] - the acceptance's facts:{evaluated:1} is not reachable keyless (no evaluation can succeed without Python), so the test pins {evaluated:0} + eval_failed:1. (2) Acceptance 3 is read at the next step's progress tick ('ranked'), since the same run then overwrites the stored outcome with 'promoted'; eval_failed and the three material warnings CARRY FORWARD to later steps, sourcing_failed/candidates_skipped stay with the publish step. (3) lifecycleDetailView takes an optional stage and falls back to prose when the stored outcome describes a stage the row has left (closed, approved after routed_to_human) - this is what keeps 'closed/redesigned rows keep rendering their detail' true without clearing outcome_json on every human write. (4) Material warnings are derived from the case AS FROZEN (scenario/seed/baseline source !== 'llm' or absent), not from this run's flags, so a resume that skips the freeze still reports them; the three *_failed exception audits map to the same warnings. (5) awaiting_submissions is written only when a collecting row has no outcome yet (pre-migration rows gain a coded line); halts/cancels now persist detail+outcome (guarded by expectedStage) where they previously only returned. (6) Wrote the outcome module ONLY as a type import from the orchestrator and db/devcase.ts (no module added to the task-hub graph); no control-route change (it still serves detail only). (7) Added a source-shape pin of DevLifecycleRow in devcase-stage-outcome.test.ts.
